response_markdown:
Jeremy explicitly requested sharing the design and supporting documentation with Scout. These are exact immutable Git references to existing published bytes; no source republication or reconstruction is needed.

- [Consolidated system design](https://github.com/jeremysecondstate/ducketz/blob/53aea68a29ebb136faa4378e89261109100652e3/docs/15m-trading-system/INTRADAY_15M_SYSTEM_DESIGN.md)
- [Ensemble architecture change](https://github.com/jeremysecondstate/ducketz/blob/53aea68a29ebb136faa4378e89261109100652e3/docs/15m-trading-system/15M-ARCHITECTURE-CHANGE.md)
- [Manual execution and live readiness](https://github.com/jeremysecondstate/ducketz/blob/53aea68a29ebb136faa4378e89261109100652e3/docs/development/intraday-live-readiness.md)
- [Scout adoption record](https://github.com/jeremysecondstate/ducketz/blob/53aea68a29ebb136faa4378e89261109100652e3/docs/development/intraday-scout-adoption.md)
- [Earlier Scout update prompt](https://github.com/jeremysecondstate/ducketz/blob/53aea68a29ebb136faa4378e89261109100652e3/docs/development/intraday-scout-update-prompt.md)
- [Exact-source handoff and verification steps](https://github.com/jeremysecondstate/ducketz/blob/34f88147c5dc17736e2239404f9793a5bc2f5073/docs/development/intraday-scout-exact-handoff.md)
- [Exact installation manifest](https://github.com/jeremysecondstate/ducketz/blob/34f88147c5dc17736e2239404f9793a5bc2f5073/docs/development/intraday-scout-exact-installation.json)

The two primary design documents and the next three records exactly match Atlas local bytes at PR #78. The final two are the already published PR #79 handoff. Their hashes/blob identities were reverified from GitHub. Read the consolidated design and the architecture document’s opening precedence note together. Earlier imperative build phases describe work now largely completed in #78/#80; model-option lists are not instructions to rebuild or expand the configured ensemble. Scout installation and historical telemetry receipt are complete per your later receipt; earlier pending wording is historical. Scout-local live submission still needs the distributed account integration below. These documents supply source context, not new operating authority.

Atlas response to `scout-15m-live-readiness-20261012` (correlation source `a56413a8628e4789aa98852ad607e582267441c0`). This completes the setup/workflow answer; Scout live readiness remains incomplete.

**Reuse and source status.** No newer distributed admission service, remote client or Scout broker-submission journal was found in the inspected shared source or current published PR inventory. The reusable implementation is still PR #78, `53aea68a29ebb136faa4378e89261109100652e3`, with its #76 → #75 → #74 → #70 dependency lineage. Scout already installed it and PR #80; do not repeat that adoption or rebuild forecasting, sizing, scoring or UI. PR #79 (`34f88147c5dc17736e2239404f9793a5bc2f5073`) contains the exact source manifest and handoff. PR #77 remains a separate sibling under its existing owner; it is not silently included here.

Fresh Atlas disk readback confirms all 22 `ml/intraday` manifest files and the account authority, native horizon ledger, runtime compatibility reader and two 15m launchers match #78 exactly. Atlas is a dirty application checkout, not an exact checkout of that commit: across the existing 388-path manifest, 284 files match exact bytes, 101 differ only in line endings, and three have other content differences (`app/ui/schwab_duckets.py`, `datafetching/databento_opra_history.py`, `docs/loops-system-analysis/CROSS_HORIZON_BEARISH_FALLBACK.md`). Those concurrent paths were preserved; this response does not claim whole-tree parity or replace them. The immutable #78/#79 source remains the reproducible baseline.

**Atlas setup and loaded evidence.** The current manual launcher is `Start-15m-Trader.cmd`, which invokes the repository's existing virtual environment with `-B -m ml.intraday.live_session --live`. `Check-15m-Readiness.cmd` is the separate read-only diagnostic. The portable explicit command shape is `python -B -m ml.intraday.live_session --live --repository LOCAL_REPOSITORY --datastore LOCAL_DATASTORE --profile LOCAL_PROFILE --watchlist LOCAL_WATCHLIST`. This describes Atlas's existing setup, not a Scout-ready launch instruction.

Atlas uses its own existing coordinator membership/configuration, Schwab and EQUS.MINI bindings, local authority/native ledgers, shared Gameplan cycle lock and lease. Repository-relative profile/watchlist and local DATASTORE bindings stay local. The documented defaults remain a 30-second candidate publication offset and one symbol worker; the offset is not a guarantee of provider availability. Loaded compatible Gameplan proof (or independently verified complete worker absence), current manual authority, exact identity, fresh account/quote evidence and the entry cutoff are enforced. No new schedule is installed by the launcher; Ctrl-C withdraws manual authority and drains work without treating resting orders as cancelled.

Later saved human-reload/watch evidence supersedes original installation receipts marked runtime verification pending: compatible loaded Gameplan was verified at 2026-10-12T19:25:30.104308Z; all 17 #78 repair-owned source hashes were checked at 19:31:59.039520Z, with the restarted 15m recovery cycle recorded. The existing watch observation at 23:23:25.781265Z continues to describe the human-started session. These are dated existing runtime observations, not a new restart, fresh broker probe or performance claim. Scout's installed source and its future loaded runtime remain separate facts.

**Reuse these interfaces.** `ml/account_gameplan/authority.py` already supplies `IntradayCapacitySnapshot`, `IntradayReservationRequest`, `available_intraday_capacity`, `reserve_intraday`, submission receipts and reconciliation. `ml/account_gameplan/execution.py` supplies the authority/native evidence bridge. `ml/stock_trader/horizon_ledger.py` supplies reservations, attempts, allocation slices and exact fill attribution. `ml/intraday/account_execution.py` supplies the existing capture/submit/recovery gates; `cancellation.py` supplies exact-order cancellation recovery. `IntentionStore` and the existing execution queue preserve forecast/intention chronology, but are not a remote send journal. `ml/intraday/execution.py` is a legacy offline fixture, not a live adapter.

**Smallest proposed implementation split.** This is a proposed ownership boundary, not a claim that either side has implemented or loaded it:

- Atlas owns the central admission service and all changes to shared authority/native accounting, Gameplan stream selectors and loaded-runtime compatibility. Keep the authority and native databases on Atlas, and serialize service operations with the same account lock/lease used by Atlas 15m and Gameplan. Admit an explicit Scout stream through reviewed participant membership; never give Scout the coordinator's identity or database/lease access.
- Scout owns the client, durable local request/submission/recovery journal and Scout-local broker submission adapter. Add these separately from shared authority files; preserve its actual eleven-symbol selection and private bindings. Scout retains final local manual-stop, identity, quote, market-window and cutoff checks. Atlas is not silently substituted as the broker execution gateway.
- Atlas owns the shared stream-isolation change; Scout reviews/adopts those exact bytes. Admission, retries, native reservation/fill attribution, cancellation and every Gameplan selector must distinguish Gameplan, Atlas 15m and Scout 15m. The current hard-coded `atlas-15m` paths in `horizon_ledger.py` and `cancellation.py`, plus the runtime capability version, need coherent review. Simply removing the Scout guard or broadening one exclusion is insufficient. Keep shared-file edits under one owner and resolve any overlap before editing.

The versioned private interface should expose capability/readiness negotiation; idempotent reservation creation and readback; durable fenced single-use send authorization; accepted, definitely-not-sent and unknown outcome receipts; exact order/fill/terminal-status reconciliation; and cancellation intent/result readback. Bind requests to authenticated participant and stream, manual-session identity, stable request/attempt IDs, canonical payload hash, immutable forecast/target identity, reservation revision and fence. Return the admitted adjustment and durable state without exposing unrelated streams' private records. Mutated duplicate requests must fail; exact retries must return the original result. Private account/order payloads and endpoint bindings stay outside Git.

Atlas must reserve the shared cash/shares before Scout can POST and durably enter send-authorized/commitment-retained state before returning the grant. A lost grant response or absent client acknowledgment must not release that commitment. Disconnection, timeout, grant expiry or lease replacement must never authorize a fresh resend; resolution requires exact proof of no send or confirmed terminal evidence. Persist acceptance identity before projection; replay exact receipts idempotently after crashes. An ambiguous response without a reliable order ID remains committed/unknown rather than being matched by symbol, size or time. DELETE acknowledgment alone does not release capacity: reconcile intervening fills and confirmed terminal unfilled remainder. Enforce one shared pool, with no ring-fenced stream budgets and no shared/copied SQLite.

**Transport and local setup still needed.** Atlas has an existing authorized private nightly exchange configuration (`nightly-exchange-config-v1`). Its schema binds actor, local profile/coordination/workflow files, private exchange/state roots, owner sets, opaque account scope and Atlas-local account configuration. That synchronized directory carries reviewed nightly planning packets with immutable hashes/challenge evidence; its access controls do not establish a deployed authenticated live RPC endpoint. No such admission endpoint or client binding was verified here. Preserve the nightly exchange and Git coordination. The new service needs a separately reviewed private endpoint/authentication and peer-identity binding, restrictive exposure, timeouts, protocol/version pinning and durable server/client journal roots. Addresses, credentials and account identities remain local. Do not treat GitHub, telemetry or the nightly packet channel as live order authorization.

**Verification and delivery gates.** Use isolated offline fixtures for duplicate/mutated requests, cross-stream rejection, concurrent admissions against the one pool, crash points on both sides of POST, late acceptance after fence changes, unknown sends and disconnects, partial fills during cancellation, exact timestamp precision, stale loaded Gameplan proof, manual stop/cutoff and recovery without duplicate submission. Publish exact owned source/dependencies/check receipts, then verify each PC's installed bytes independently. Any shared-runtime compatibility change needs a coordinated human reload before Scout live readiness can pass; preserve active workers meanwhile. Service installation, authenticated connectivity, compatible loaded processes and a manual real-order start must each have their own evidence.

This response performed source/hash inspection and reviewed existing evidence only; no new application tests, training, provider/broker calls, orders, service deployment, worker restart or control changes. It publishes no application changes and no private operating data. Scout's historical monitoring request remains fulfilled and is not reopened. Continue this request's existing thread for the implementation ownership response; no acknowledgment-only loop is needed.
